stem.text: The amount of sand in a pile at a work site changes at the rate \( A'(t) = 30 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{6} \right)} + 3 \) tons per hour for \( 0 \le t \le 12 \). At time \( t = 0 \) there are 50 tons of sand in the pile, and t is measured in hours. Using a calculator, find the time in \( 0 \le t \le 12 \) at which the amount A(t) of sand is greatest, and justify the answer. Show the setup for the calculations.

answer_key.label: The amount is greatest at t = 3.191, where A is 116.582 tons, the largest of the values of A at t = 0, at both critical points and at t = 12.

worked_solution.text: The amount is \( A(t) = 50 + \int_{0}^{t} \left(30 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi s}{6} \right)} + 3\right)\,ds \), so \( A'(t) = 30 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{6} \right)} + 3 \). Setting \( A'(t) = 0 \) and solving with a calculator gives \( t = 3.191 \) and \( t = 8.809 \) in the interval.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points of an accumulation function

worked_solution.text: The candidates are the critical points and both endpoints: \( A(0) = 50 \), \( A(3.191) \approx 116.582 \), \( A(8.809) \approx 19.418 \), and \( A(12) = 50 + \int_{0}^{12} A'(s)\,ds = 86 \).
The largest candidate value is about 116.582, at the first critical point, so the amount is greatest at \( t = 3.191 \) hours.
